definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: a hunky man

blocks.note: first meaning: one of a troupe of muscular male strippers famous for that name
second meaning: Thomas, the eighteenth-century English furniture designer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a historic furniture craftsman was a good-looking, muscular fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chippendales are a famous male striptease troupe; Thomas Chippendale was the great Georgian furniture maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The same surname names both a famous dancing troupe of muscular men and a celebrated Georgian furniture craftsman.

clue.text: It makes for a protracted smoking habit

definitions.text: It makes for a protracted smoking habit

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who keeps on smoking for years
setter's reading: a device that physically lengthens what is smoked

explanation.surface: Something is blamed for turning a person into a long-term smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protracted' suggests a habit lasting a long time, but it means literally drawn out in length: the tube puts distance between the lips and the cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: This slim tube extends the cigarette's length, so the act of smoking literally becomes longer.

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
Time is an example of a magazine, MAG for short

explanation.surface: A photograph is said to be about time, perhaps as a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks hint that Time is a title: the American news magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a visual representation, which is exactly what this word for a likeness means.

indicators.note: something foreign is strange and unfamiliar, so these letters appear in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Foreign dishes are being praised as pleasant cookery.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the French city, which fits 'foreign', but it is the old sense of nice: fine, exacting, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense nice means finely discriminating or exact, a synonym of accurate and particular.

clue.text: Greek goddess in charge of deserts

definitions.text: Greek goddess in charge of deserts

blocks.note: surface reading: a deity ruling over sandy wastelands
setter's reading: what people deserve, as in just deserts

explanation.surface: A Greek deity is said to rule over the world's arid wastelands.
explanation.walkthrough: Deserts is pronounced like desserts here and means what one deserves; this goddess dealt out retribution.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the Greek goddess of retribution, punishing arrogance by giving people the fate they had earned.

clue.text: The animal found furthest from zoo

definitions.text: The animal found furthest from zoo

blocks.clueFragment: The animal found furthest from zoo
blocks.note: surface reading: a creature living far away from any zoo
setter's reading: in alphabetical order, the beast at the far end of the dictionary from the word zoo

explanation.surface: Some wild creature is described as living a long way from captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: Think of a dictionary: zoo sits near the very end, and this burrowing African anteater is one of the first entries.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting with a double A, this African burrowing mammal stands at the head of the alphabet, as remote from Z as possible.

blocks.note: surface reading: weather charts forecasting bad weather
setter's reading: a brainstorm, so the locations are in the head

explanation.surface: Meteorologists draw charts showing where bad weather might strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The storm is a brainstorm, so these maps trace activity in the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: These are recordings of electrical activity in the brain, which is where any brainstorm would happen.

clue.text: (and 16) Determined to remain a committed bachelor?

definitions.note: defines the full linked answer with 16, single-minded
defines the full linked answer with 16, minded to stay single

blocks.note: first meaning of the two-part answer: resolutely focused on one aim
second meaning, read literally: inclined to stay unmarried

explanation.surface: A man is resolved never to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: This entry and 16 together make SINGLE-MINDED. Split the phrase: someone minded to stay single is literally of that mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means resolutely focused on one goal, and taken literally means having a mind to stay unmarried.

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks its structure, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Invading throngs are laying waste to the Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are large, unruly multitudes, originally nomadic raiding tribes such as the Mongols.

clue.text: Goneril, for example, makes it with Regan

indicators.note: makes here means forms or constructs, so the following letters are built into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: One of Lear's wicked daughters teams up with her sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Goneril and Regan are King Lear's two ungrateful daughters in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril repays her father's generosity with cruelty, making her an example of an ungrateful person.

blocks.note: first meaning: the North African kingdom
second meaning: fine goatskin used for bookbinding

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one idea, rustic leather, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a North African kingdom and also a soft goatskin tanned with sumac, used for bindings.

indicators.note: exotic means strange and outlandish, so the letters are given an unusual order
among means in the midst of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, including the s
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tourist singles out one of the tropical flowers growing on the Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: These are fragrant white-flowered shrubs, a kind of plant often grown in greenhouses and gardens.

clue.text: Flat heads of valves and plugs in dynamos

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: An electrician's complaint: the valves and plugs in the dynamos have gone flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat sounds like an electrical term beside valves and dynamos, but it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat in the sense of lifeless and uninteresting is a synonym of insipid or dull.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their place and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes the cuisine found in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, grub or a meal is called by this plural slang term for things to eat.

clue.text: Throws a banquet in the garden

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: flower beds make up a garden
a spread is a lavish meal laid out

explanation.surface: Someone hosts a lavish outdoor dinner party among the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Throws looks like a verb, as in throwing a party, but it is a noun: blankets cast over furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A throw is a decorative blanket or cover, and these coverlets laid over beds are an example.

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so the letters are blended into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A geologist notes the coarse texture of a lump of fool's gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Pyrites is fool's gold, a chemical compound of iron and sulphur, which makes the surface sound scientific.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means harshness or unevenness, of surface or of temper, from the Latin for rough.

indicators.note: forms means shapes, so the letters are moulded into another shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A potter moulds pots every summer season.
explanation.walkthrough: Clay suggests pottery, but here it is a clay pipe: this soft white mineral is carved into tobacco pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a soft white clay-like mineral, and also the name for a tobacco pipe carved from it.

definitions.note: cross-reference: this is the second half of the answer clued at 7

blocks.note: the clue lives at 7 down, which defines the two-word phrase as a whole

explanation.walkthrough: This light holds the second half of SINGLE-MINDED; the definition and wordplay are all at 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Together with the entry at seven it forms a phrase meaning resolutely determined on one purpose.

clue.text: Look inside the last bit of cheese for a parasite

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

blocks.note: the heel is the hard end piece of a cheese or loaf
an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Someone is told to check the rind of a cheese for a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: This hair-thin worm lives as a parasite inside insects before emerging into water as an adult.

clue.text: The tail end of a decapitated dormouse cut up

indicators.note: decapitated means the head is cut off, so the opening letter goes
something cut up is chopped into pieces and jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene: the rear half of a beheaded rodent, chopped into bits.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail end looks like the deletion signal, but it is the definition: a zoological term for the hind body.
explanation.definitionFit: In zoology this names the posterior segments of an arthropod's body, its abdominal or rear section.

blocks.note: surface reading: terrifying, as of fearsome jaws
setter's reading: a toothed grooming tool literally lifts the hair

explanation.surface: Something has frightening teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair-raising means scary but is read literally; the clue prints "It's" where "Its" is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: This grooming tool has a row of teeth that are drawn through the hair, lifting and tidying it.

blocks.note: first meaning: a financial supporter, especially of a theatre production
second meaning, whimsically: one who goes backwards

explanation.surface: A heavenly being is pictured falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre slang an angel is an investor; the question mark flags the made-up sense of one who backs away.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is slang for a sponsor who funds a show, and a supporter of that kind is a financial investor.

clue.text: The hangman used it at the end...

definitions.text: The hangman used it at the end...

blocks.clueFragment: The hangman used it at the end
blocks.note: surface reading: something a hangman resorted to finally
setter's reading: the rope loop sits at the end of the rope

explanation.surface: An executioner turned to something in the final moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue, as if a story about Houdini's escapes continues.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the loop with a running knot tied at the end of a rope, used by an executioner.

clue.text: ...all the same, he set Houdini some tricks to get out of

indicators.note: the letters are to be extracted from within the run of words before it

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: An executioner challenges the great escapologist with a series of tricky escapes.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of the escapologist's name through to the middle of tricks. All the same is not 'nevertheless' but 'of equal measure'.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix iso means equal and metric means measure, so the word describes things of the same dimensions.

clue.text: Taken in, but not quite defeated

indicators.note: not quite means falling short of whole, so a letter is missing

blocks.note: to be defeated is to be beaten

explanation.surface: Someone was deceived, though not entirely beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter is the one dropped here. Taken in suggests being fooled, but it means swallowed, as food is.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed and swallowed has been taken into the body.

indicators.note: blowing suggests being tossed around by a gale, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor notices a gale pushing the ship backwards, rear end first.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means with the end pointing forwards, so a ship moving stern first travels that way.

indicators.note: rewritten means set down again differently, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet keeps redrafting a two-line verse over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means multiplied by eight, from the Latin octo, the way double means multiplied by two.

blocks.note: surface reading: a sport the monarch enjoys
setter's reading: the original indoor court game of kings, named for its royal patrons

explanation.surface: Someone asks what sport the monarch plays.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the ancient indoor racquet game, also called real tennis, played at Hampton Court since Henry VIII's time.
explanation.definitionFit: The old court game earned its regal name from patronage by kings, so a monarch playing it fits.
